Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 How to Play 3 End of the Round 4 End of the Game 5 Scoring Overview The game is a little like Carcasonne, but simpler (and more colorful). You get points for the different things you put in your village (visitors, stalls, balloons, etc.) as long as the path it's on (either paved path or blooming trail) is connected to your starting tile. How to Play 1. Take a tile from the board The tile must be at either end of either row. 2. Place the tile in your village When you select a tile, dotted squares will appear in your village to indicate where you can place the tile. Once you've chosen a location, you can rotate the tile however you want. But to score points, an element must be on a path/trail connected to La Catrina (your starting tile). Once you have three balloons of the same color connected to your starting tile, you get the top Balloon Tile of that color. It will score at the end of the game. When you have six of that color, the Balloon Tile will flip to score even more points. To attract chimeras, you build pedestals (yellow stone altars). There are two legal sizes of pedestals: 2x2 and 2x5. When you place two stalls of the same type in your village, you immediately take an additional Path Tile and place it. You may be able to chain this during the same turn, depending on which tiles you draw. End of the Round When the last path tile is taken from the board, the round ends. Refill the board and the Catrina token goes to the next player. End of the Game Once a player takes and places the last tile, the game ends. The game lasts for as many rounds as there are players. When all rounds are completed, the score for each village is tallied. Scoring Remember, elements must be on a path leading back to your La Catrina to be counted. Element Points Notes Visitor 1 point Butterfly 2 points Balloon Tile Varies depending on tile Balloons themselves are not worth points, but balloons of the same color gain Balloon Tiles Chimera 2x2 = 3 points Altars must be closed and the exact size needed 2x5 = 5 points Stall 1 Stall = 0 points There are six types of stalls 2 Stalls = 1 point 3 Stalls = 4 points 4 Stalls = 9 points 5 Stalls = 16 points 6 Stalls = 25 points Altar 1 x [element] Each altar scores for a different element (e.g., blue balloons, butterflies, stalls) Board Game Arena would like to thank The Flying Games for making it possible to have this game here. 2405 vivacatrina العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 3.1/10] Un Carcassone bourré d’icônes. C'est tellement formaté, vu , revu et rerevu. Le jeu est oublié avant même que la partie soit finie.  La mécanique de double rivière grignotable des 2 coté est pas mal. Mais à quoi bon un moteur correct pour des objectifs aussi inintéressants ?

[Rating: 4/10] after 1 game on BGA: A very simple tile placement game with colorful artwork and a refreshing theme. Compared to other tile placement games like Carcassonne or Carmague, however, this one lacks meaningful decisions or surprising twists. Even in a two-player game I found the downtime boring – and with more players it probably only gets worse. Which tile to pick next is usually pretty obvious. Since everyone builds their own individual tableau, it even has less potential for meaningful interaction than the already rather mild Carcassonne. In the end, it just leaves me shrugging.

[Rating: 4/10] Nice looking, but nothing here excites me. Scoring is vanilla and there’s no twist to it either. And I abhor the manner in which the tiles are drafted. You can find much better options that play similarly.

[Rating: 5/10] A point salad tile laying game where players are trying to place tiles for points across many scoring criteria.
